matches.rationale: The ground-truth defect is the paper's core mis-assumption that galaxies occupy a different reference frame than the observer, requiring an SR-aberration correction to cosmological distances. Findings 1 and 2 directly attack this premise (the invalid velocity/covector derivation and the double-counting of aberration on top of already-encoded null-geodesic optics), while findings 3 and 4 identify the downstream distance-formula and phase-space-measure errors that are the direct mathematical consequence of applying this erroneous frame assumption, matching the GT's claim of 'flawed equations and invalid results throughout the paper'.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Directly identifies the invalid velocity derivation underlying the false relative-frame assumption for galaxies.
Shows the SR aberration correction double-counts geometry already encoded in the null-geodesic distance, the core manifestation of the frame-mismatch error.
Identifies the resulting distortion of luminosity/angular distance definitions caused by the same flawed frame-based derivation.
Flags the invalid invariant-measure argument used to justify the same erroneous aberration/frame treatment.
Points out a sign/formula inconsistency in the H(z) expansion function, a separate arithmetic issue not tied to the reference-frame defect.
Identifies an independent inconsistency in solving for r1 and the flat-curvature limit, unrelated to the reference-frame assumption defect.
